# Olaf Scholz in 2024: initial evidence note

2024 reads as a mixed-to-negative year for Scholz’s term. The dominant 2024 events were domestic instability, coalition collapse, and a failed confidence vote. The main favorable material is foreign-policy continuity on Ukraine and some macroeconomic stabilization signals early in the year, though the year still ended with recession and political breakdown.

## Accepted claims

| Type | Source title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs / lens |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| 2024 event | Regierungserklärung von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz | Bundesregierung | 13 Nov 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/suche/regierungserklaerung-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2320314 | Scholz told the Bundestag he had dismissed Finance Minister Christian Lindner, said the decision was necessary, and linked it to moving toward early elections. This is strong evidence of coalition breakdown and weakened governing authority in 2024. | 8B.* effectiveness / governing capacity |
| 2024 event | Deutschland coalition collapses: what comes next? | Reuters (via Investing.com) | 6 Nov 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936 | Reuters reported that Scholz fired Lindner, causing the governing coalition to collapse and triggering political chaos in Germany’s largest economy. This is direct evidence of domestic instability under Scholz in 2024. | 8B.* effectiveness / domestic stability |
| 2024 event | Vertrauensfrage und vorzeitige Neuwahlen | Deutscher Bundestag | 16 Dec 2024 | https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw47-vertrauensfrage-1030198 | The Bundestag withheld confidence from Scholz by a large margin, opening the way for snap elections. This is a concrete indicator that his parliamentary authority had collapsed by year-end. | 8B.* effectiveness / parliamentary control |

This reinforces the picture of a chancellorship that entered managed termination rather than stable continuation. | 8B.* effectiveness / regime stability |

This is favorable evidence for foreign-policy consistency and crisis management. | foreign-policy effectiveness / security leadership |

This is a favorable partial macroeconomic indicator, but it does not offset the recession and coalition crisis. | economic management / cost-of-living |

## Bottom line

- Strong negative evidence in 2024: coalition collapse, loss of confidence in parliament, and a weak economic year.
- Strong favorable evidence in 2024: continued high-profile support for Ukraine and some disinflation / stabilization versus 2022-2023.
- Best overall reading from the sources above: Scholz’s 2024 term looked politically brittle at home, more credible on foreign policy than on domestic governing effectiveness.
